questions.stem: In organ procurement, when does cold ischaemic time start?
options: When the organ is implanted and warms up
When the donor's arterial line trace goes flat
At aortic cross-clamp or cold preservation flush
When the organ is removed from the donor

questions.stem: What is the cold ischaemic time limit for the heart in organ procurement?
Why must a donor heart be reimplanted quickly after cold storage?
What is the cold ischaemic time limit for lungs in organ procurement?
What is the cold ischaemic time limit for the liver in organ procurement?
Why does longer cold ischaemic time matter for a donor liver?
questions.answer: Raises risk of ischaemic cholangiopathy (bile duct injury)

questions.stem: What is the cold ischaemic time limit for the pancreas in organ procurement?
Why is prolonged cold ischaemia a concern for a donor pancreas?
What is the cold ischaemic time limit for the kidney in organ procurement?
Why can a donor kidney tolerate long cold ischaemic times?
questions.answer: Low metabolic demand when it is not filtering

questions.stem: In organ transplantation, what is warm ischaemic time (WIT)?
questions.answer: Time at body temperature with blood supply stopped or reduced

questions.stem: In organ implantation, what marks the end of warm ischaemic time?
What is the warm ischaemic time limit for the heart in transplantation?
What is the warm ischaemic time limit per lung in transplantation?
What is the warm ischaemic time limit for the liver in transplantation?
In transplantation, the warm ischaemic time limit for the kidney is ____.
In donation after circulatory death, what is the extra donor warm ischaemic period?
questions.answer: Unavoidable warm ischaemia before cold perfusion begins

questions.stem: In DCD donors, what does the agonal phase cover?
questions.answer: From start of treatment withdrawal to cessation of cardiac output

questions.stem: In DCD donors, what does absolute warm ischaemic time run between?
questions.answer: Cardiac arrest to start of the cold flush

questions.stem: In DCD donors, when does functional donor warm ischaemic time start?
questions.answer: When donor perfusion falls below a set limit

Which ischaemic timer starts at the cold flush or cross-clamp in organ procurement?

options: When the organ starts to warm during implantation

questions.stem: In donation after brain death, the donor may need ____ blood for retrieval.
How is anaesthetic drug use during brain-dead donor retrieval regarded?
In brain-dead donor retrieval, what is the aim of anaesthesia regarding spinal reflexes?
questions.answer: Block haemodynamic and motor responses from spinal reflexes

questions.stem: Why may opioids alone be inadequate during brain-dead donor retrieval?
questions.answer: They may not control catecholamine surges from surgical stimulation

questions.stem: In donation after brain death, continue ICU ____ care.
What heparin dose is given to brain-dead donors before aortic cross-clamp?
How long before aortic cross-clamp is heparin given to brain-dead donors?
Through which access is heparin given to a brain-dead donor before cross-clamp?
In brain-dead donor retrieval, when are the ventilator and monitors switched off?
questions.answer: Once the aorta is clamped and cold flush starts

questions.stem: In brain-dead donor retrieval, what is the usual order of organ removal?
After organ removal in brain-dead donation, where is the deceased sent?
In DCD donation, which warm ischaemic time measure applies to the donor?
In DCD, what happens if the agonal plus no-touch period is too long?
What does withdrawal of care involve in DCD donation?
In DCD, how long is the no-touch period after a flat arterial line trace?
In DCD donation, how many certifiers must certify death?
In DCD donation, within what window must death occur?
What is the purpose of organ-preserving CPR?
questions.answer: To preserve organs for donation, not to revive the patient

questions.stem: What can organ-preserving CPR do for patients and families?
What is a drawback of aggressive organ-preserving CPR?
questions.answer: May injure the patient and cause psychological harm to families and staff
